acceptance: The margin report of go/cmd/testlatency (make print-test-timeout-darwin, -timeout-margin) shows at least 10m of margin for cmd/evolve on the macOS job of the PR that makes the change
A test in cmd/testlatency or the package wall ratchet fails when a darwin package margin falls below a threshold that policy data holds
No timeout or ratchet number is raised
fix: Find the slowest cmd/evolve tests on darwin (the margin report from cmd/testlatency), and cut their cost or move them to their own package so that the slowest package has a margin of at least a third of the timeout on the slowest runner seen. Do not raise DARWIN_TEST_TIMEOUT without operator approval.
summary: On 2026-11-24 the macOS job of PRs 1789 and 1790 failed with panic: test timed out after 30m0s in go/cmd/evolve, inside TestCLIContract_HarnessKillsEachMutantOfDossierShow. Both passed on a rerun of the failed job. The macOS job of main (the whole job, not the package alone) took 14, 20 and 32 minutes on three commits in a row, so runner speed varies by more than two times, and cmd/evolve reaches the 30m DARWIN_TEST_TIMEOUT on a slow runner. The package wall ratchet measures speed-adjusted CPU, so it does not catch a wall-clock overrun on a slow runner. Every batch PR is at risk of a false red. On 2026-11-26 it recurred two more times: on main a3b1f16d5 and on PR #1841, with the write-cwd, write-in-home and write-in-tmpdir subtests of TestCLIContract_HarnessKillsEachMutantOfDossierShow running at the panic (about 1m39s each). Both went green on a re-run. Incident record: docs/incidents/2026-11-26-cmd-evolve-darwin-suite-at-the-30m-limit.md.
title: The cmd/evolve darwin tests stay well inside the go test timeout on a slow macOS runner
